security_audit.summary: The audit confirms high-risk offensive content in the skill, including privilege escalation, shell escape, persistence, credential discovery, and firmware extraction workflows. Several noisy Markdown and /dev/null detections were dismissed, but the remaining confirmed findings support a critical security posture. No prompt injection text was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Remove instructions for adding root users, SSH authorized keys, reverse shells, or startup persistence.

remediation.issue: Privilege escalation and shell escape recipes
remediation.suggestion: Replace exploit steps with safe validation guidance and require explicit authorization before any invasive action.
Remove directions to access password files, sudoers, private keys, API keys, or credential search paths.

remediation.issue: Firmware dumping and network transfer examples
remediation.suggestion: Limit firmware workflows to owned lab devices and avoid network transfer to attacker-style endpoints.

remediation.issue: Session logs stored in shared temporary paths
remediation.suggestion: Default logs to a user-selected protected directory and require restrictive permissions for sensitive sessions.

content.value_statement: UART console testing requires careful serial setup, logging, and device command handling. This skill guides authorized IoT analysis with picocom, a Python helper, and structured session review.
actual_capabilities: Configure picocom and serial_helper.py for UART device sessions.
Run single, interactive, and batch serial commands with prompt detection.
Capture serial session logs and observe them in another terminal.
Guide device enumeration from bootloader, login, or shell prompts.
Explain common BusyBox, U-Boot, and serial troubleshooting patterns.
Support firmware analysis workflows for authorized test devices.
limitations: Requires physical UART access and user-granted serial permissions.
Does not verify legal authorization for a target device.
May expose credentials if logs are stored in shared locations.
Includes offensive testing workflows that need strict lab controls.

use_cases.title: Bring Up a UART Session
use_cases.description: Set baud rate, serial device path, prompt detection, and logging for a known test board.

use_cases.title: Document Device Enumeration
use_cases.description: Collect authorized system, firmware, and service observations from a serial shell for reporting.

use_cases.title: Monitor Long Serial Runs
use_cases.description: Log and observe serial interactions while another process performs controlled command execution.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Basic Session
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a connected UART adapter.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me open an authorized UART session on /dev/ttyUSB0 at 115200 baud and save a protected session log.

prompt_templates.title: Identify the Prompt
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt detection for a known device.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the serial helper to connect to my lab device, detect the prompt, and explain the next safe enumeration steps.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Session Log
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this authorized serial log and summarize boot events, shell access state, services, and follow-up validation questions.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Controlled Assessment
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a UART assessment plan for my owned IoT device, including setup, evidence handling, safe commands, and reporting checkpoints.

output_examples.input: I connected a USB serial adapter and need to start testing.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends confirming the device path, selecting the baud rate, enabling logging, and checking for a stable prompt before enumeration.

output_examples.input: I have a serial log from a boot sequence.
output_examples.output: The skill can summarize bootloader messages, kernel details, login prompts, visible services, and evidence that needs authorization review.

output_examples.input: My serial output has command echoes and ANSI control characters.
output_examples.output: The helper workflow can clean command output, remove prompt noise, and keep a chronological log for later analysis.

best_practices: Use the skill only on devices you own or have explicit permission to test.
Store serial logs in protected locations because they may contain secrets.
Prefer read-only enumeration until test scope and recovery steps are clear.
anti_patterns: Do not use the workflows against third-party devices or networks without written authorization.
Do not store credential-bearing logs in shared temporary directories.
Do not add persistence, backdoor access, or account changes during routine testing.

faq.question: Does it require hardware access?

faq.question: Can it run commands on a device?
faq.answer: Yes, when a serial shell is available. Commands should stay within the approved test scope.

faq.question: Can it analyze logs?
faq.answer: Yes. It can help interpret serial logs, boot output, prompts, and command results.

faq.question: Is it safe for automatic installation?
faq.answer: The audit should decide that separately because the skill includes offensive security workflows.
